prerequisites: The TFG must be defended and evaluated once it has been reliably confirmed that the student has passed all remaining subjects of the study plan and, therefore, has all the necessary credits for obtaining the Degree title, except those corresponding to the TFG itself.

learning_outcomes.text: General presentation: adequacy to standards, legibility, writing, spelling, etc.
Logical and coherent structure in the representation of information, ideas, and arguments.
Interest of the author's points of view, judgments, and conclusions.
Quality of the presentation: appropriate use of media, correctness of oral expression, logical structuring, adequacy to available time, etc.
Ability to engage and capture the audience's attention.
Synthesize and integrate the competencies acquired in the teachings, covering general competencies CG1 to CG9, and specific competencies depending on the work's theme.

syllabus_topics: Topics related to the area of Engineering in which the student has completed their studies, as indicated in the objectives of each degree.

assessment_methods.method: Monitoring of student's face-to-face activities by their academic tutor
Final document presented by the student
Public presentation of the work before the tribunal and subsequent debate

assessment_rules: The Bachelor's Thesis must be presented and defended before a university tribunal. The evaluation will generally consider the monitoring of the student's face-to-face activities by their academic tutor, the final document presented by the student, and the public presentation of the work before the tribunal and subsequent debate. The final definition of the evaluation system will comply with the regulations defined in the Bachelor's Thesis Regulations of the School of Engineering. Both ordinary and extraordinary evaluations are conducted through a public presentation before a tribunal of three professors.
